Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: colleague
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and another person who is their colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John colleague Jane", "Professor Smith colleague 'https://example.com/prof-jones'". Distinct from colleagues, which is a plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: teaches
candidates.comment: An educational relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is designed to teach. Also called "educates on", "imparts knowledge of", "instructs in", "covers topic". Examples: "The course teaches 'Algebra'", "The learning resource teaches problem-solving skills", "This event teaches advanced programming concepts."

candidates.label: educationalRole
candidates.comment: An educational role relation between an educational audience and the text describing its specific role. Also called "audience role", "learner role", "student type". Examples: "Educational audience educationalRole 'Student'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Teacher'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Parent'".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: termDuration
candidates.comment: A duration representing the length of a term of study within an educational or occupational program. Also called "term length", "semester duration", "quarter length", "study period duration". Examples: "The program has termDuration 15 weeks", "The educational program's termDuration is 10 weeks", "This course has a termDuration of one semester."

candidates.label: memberOf

Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: member

Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: musicGroupMember
candidates.comment: A person who is a member of a music group. Also called band member, group member, musician in group. Examples: "The Beatles musicGroupMember 'John Lennon'", "Queen musicGroupMember 'Freddie Mercury'", "Fleetwood Mac musicGroupMember 'Stevie Nicks'". Distinct from member, which is a general property for any organization.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.
